contributions.statement: For cross-service flow or authorization review in Java microservices, expose a few typed, compiler-grade static-analysis queries (call graph, data flow, entry-point and sink lookup, e.g. via CodeQL) as agent tools and reserve the LLM for semantic judgments such as which operation is privileged and whether the authZ check is adequate.
contributions.evidence: §VI-C/D, Tables V and VII: removing the query primitives drops recall to 4.8%; Neo reaches 81% precision / 85% recall on a ground-truth set and beats a bash-based agent (EnIGMA). Audit: ablation recall is computed over vulnerabilities Neo itself found (near-circular), and EnIGMA was run with Neo's prompts.

contributions.statement: Link services across repos by matching channel identifiers (REST route templates, gRPC methods, Kafka/RabbitMQ topic names) so an agent can follow a flow from producer to consumer.
contributions.evidence: §IV inter-service channel queries over REST/gRPC/Kafka/RabbitMQ/Dubbo in 25 apps; audit notes Q_inter is never ablated and the services sit in one repository.

reason: Peer-reviewed, Java-heavy polyglot evidence for 'deterministic analysis retrieves, LLM judges semantics', with an ablation (if partly circular). The cross-service channel linking is a useful, untested idea for multi-repo work.
